text:
Amazon has signed four Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) in Sweden with French sustainable investment manager Mirova and Swedish renewable firm OX2 for around 200MW of capacity.
Three of the PPAs are tied to the Saena portfolio, which comprises three onshore wind farms developed by Swedish renewable developer Eolus AB and acquired by Mirova last year. The PPAs will see Amazon offtake 17.5MW from the Boarp wind farm in Jönköping Municipality, 18MW from the Dållebo wind farm in Ulricehamn, Västra Götaland County, and 31.5MW from the Fagelas wind farm in Västra Götaland, western Sweden. Combined, the sites will deliver 67MW of power to Amazon and are all already operational.
The final PPA is tied to the 189-MW Fagerasen wind farm in Dalarna County, with Amazon agreeing to offtake 132MW from the project. Eolus AB and Dala Vind AB developed the wind farm, and OX2 AB acquired it last year. It is currently under construction, with commercial operations slated for sometime in 2028.
Amazon currently operates a cloud region in Stockholm, which it launched back in 2018. The company has backed several sustainability initiatives in Sweden, including a water replenishment project and a green steel initiative with SSAB.
The deal with OX2 builds on an established partnership between the two companies. In April last year, Amazon signed two PPAs with OX2 in Finland for the entire capacity of the 367MW Rajamäenkylä wind farm located in Isojoki and Karijoki municipalities and the 105MW Honkakangas wind farm in Halsua.
Following this, in November, the firms inked a 28MW PPA in Poland for power from the Annopol wind park in Lublin Voivodeship in the southeast of the country. The site is currently expected to go online sometime in 2027.
